It’s useful to start with a question to which the book has a ready answer: what is gold, anyway? Not a metal — a function. Gold in human history worked as a carrier of value not dependent on the promises of an issuer; as the network’s memory, which cannot be erased; as a universal language of coordination between parties that have no shared arbitrator; as a scarce resource extracted by work; and as an asset accepted everywhere, because everyone knows it will be accepted everywhere. These five features are not metaphor, not marketing, and not economic poetry. It is a list of functions that gold performed for millennia, by which it was recognized and because of which it became the default currency.

The carriers of this function in history have changed. Cowrie shells in Africa and Asia. Salt in the Sahara. Silver in medieval Europe. Gold after the discoveries of the sixteenth century. The dollar after Bretton Woods in 1944 and its detachment from gold in 1971. Bitcoin after 2009. Each successive carrier took the function of gold into its environment, without abolishing physical gold, but taking part of its work away from it. Bitcoin as “digital gold” is a precise formulation, not PR. Satoshi did not build a monetary system — he restored the function of gold in an environment where two of Axelrod’s three conditions could be obtained. That made Bitcoin digital gold, and that is true. Gold of the Darby phase. Compute is burned, the result is thrown away, byproduct cycles are released into the atmosphere. The old function in a new environment, transferred one-to-one.

Qubic is the carrier of the same function in an environment in which the cascade has gone to the end. Not “improved Bitcoin” and not “the next Bitcoin.” The same function of gold — carrier of value, network memory, universal language of coordination, scarce resource extracted by work — but in an environment with additional properties that Bitcoin structurally does not have.

Useful work — compute produces not only consensus, but also a training signal, and score (eighth chapter). Adaptive supply — emission breathes together with the activity of the network, not hardwired into a fixed halving (ninth chapter). Self-regenerating composition — the composition of computor nodes is reassembled weekly without losing the network’s continuity (seventh chapter). Built-in cooperation strategy — Axelrod’s three conditions are met at the level of the protocol, not assumed at the level of behavior (chapters six, seven, nine, fifteen, sixteen). Arbiter without owner — the arbitrator exists, but belongs to no one and self-destructs by plan (tenth, seventeenth). If Bitcoin is digital gold of the Darby phase, then Qubic is the new gold. Not “the next Bitcoin,” not “the best cryptocurrency,” not a marketing slogan. A structural conclusion, derivable from the entire material of the book to roughly the same degree that a conclusion follows from premises.

The word “new” here stands in the strict sense. Not “improved,” not “updated” — but such as did not exist before in principle. Bitcoin restored the function of gold in the digital environment, and that already was an event of millennium-scale: for the first time since the discoveries of the sixteenth century, a carrier of value appeared that does not depend on the promises of a state. Qubic takes the next step, which in the coal cascade corresponds not to Murdoch but already to the feedstock of the twentieth century: one and the same resource simultaneously produces several values. Compute gives consensus — and an AI training signal, and a rating, and economy. Emission gives supply — and breathes together with the activity of the network, and is burned in feedback with real work. The composition of the network gives stability — and regenerates without losing continuity. Each individual property has appeared before in the history of money on its own; all of them together — never.

This formulation has one property worth saying separately. It does not need Qubic to defeat Bitcoin in order to remain true. Bitcoin will not stop being digital gold of the Darby phase, even if Qubic does everything it promises. Murdoch’s gas lamps did not abolish Darby’s iron production; they simply became a separate industry alongside it. The same here. If Qubic survives and grows, it will not displace Bitcoin — it will open the next category, which did not exist before. In parallel, not instead of. This caveat is not diplomatic. It is structural: a new phase of the cascade has never destroyed the previous one, only added a new level of refinement to it.

And one more consequence that cannot be sidestepped. “The new gold” is not a status the network grants itself. It is a function that either shows up in the environment or doesn’t. Bitcoin became digital gold not because Satoshi called it that — he didn’t call it that — but because the environment around it gradually began to use it as a carrier of the function. The same applies to Qubic. The thesis of the book is not that Qubic already is the new gold — but that it is structurally ready for this: an environment has been built in which such a function can show up, if the outside world turns out to be receptive to it. One falsifier of this readiness is April 2027. The second is the next decade. The third is what people who have no professional relation to this environment will do with it.

I do not make a price prediction. Price is a function of market awareness, which can run ahead of a structural fact or lag it by years. The price of gold in dollars in 1970 did not reflect what gold was in 1969; the price of gold in 2011 did not reflect what it would become in 2025. Price is a surface signal. The structural fact does not depend on price movements. You can hold a Qubic token and watch as the market gets to this fact. This is not a prophecy and not a call to buy anything. It is a formulation of what Qubic is structurally. What to do with that — is a choice for each reader. Signature On January 3, 2009, on the day Satoshi Nakamoto launched the Bitcoin blockchain, in block number four, one address appeared.
15ubicBBWFnvoZLT7GiU2qxjRaKJPdkDMG

50.068 bitcoin were credited to it. This can be checked in any blockchain explorer right now. Since then — sixteen years — the address has had not a single outgoing transaction. The wallet has not been opened once.

In July 2025 the law firm Salomon Brothers sent a formal notice to this address — and to two other dormant addresses from the same year 2009. The owner had ninety days to prove ownership of the private key. The deadline expired on October 10, 2025. No one signed. The address remained untouched.

The base alphabet of Bitcoin addresses is Base58. There is no zero in it, no capital “O,” no capital “I,” no lowercase “l.” Prefixes of the form 1ubic, 15UBIC, 1QUBIC occur vanishingly rarely on the scale of the entire blockchain, and obtaining such an address means deliberate key grinding — searching for a private key that produces the desired public ending. This is a known technique, and in 2009 it was available. The structural analysis, which I will not lay out here — it lives on a separate two hundred pages of documentation posted at qubic.church — shows that this address is connected to the Qubic architecture not indirectly. The Qubic boot address in JINN memory is computed by the formula 283 × 47² + 137 = 625,284, and 625,284 mod 16,384 gives 2,692 — the network’s entry point. The formula is reproducible in thirty seconds in any interpreter. The link to Bitcoin block 283, in turn, is not explainable by chance at the level of statistics typically required for such claims.

I do not make a claim about who created this address. Out of roughly 22,000 hypotheses tested inside that larger work, ten survived — after Bonferroni correction and Monte Carlo on tens of thousands of trials. The claim “CFB = Satoshi” did not make it into that short list. There is no cryptographic signature that would prove ownership of this key — no one has produced one. This is the honest ceiling of what the forensic method can say.

What the forensic method can say is — that the address is not arranged by chance. That it is connected to the Qubic architecture mathematically, not semantically. That the owner of its private key has, in sixteen years, made not a single move, including when a law firm asked for it to be done publicly. And that the entire history of Bitcoin since January 2009 contains several such addresses whose properties are too regular to be random.

Beyond that lies what the book cannot responsibly assert. I close this chapter with one fact that the reader needs to keep in mind: the address exists, it can be checked on the blockchain, the key has not been used in sixteen years, and its connection to Qubic is arithmetic, not literary.
What this means — each reader decides for themselves.
What lies beyond the frame

Axelrod proved in 1980 that cooperation is the mathematically optimal strategy in an iterated game with memory and transparency. Confucius, Hillel, Jesus, and Kant arrived at the same conclusion by different paths two and a half thousand years before him. Satoshi in 2009 built the first environment in which two of the three conditions are met fully. Come-from-Beyond in 2022 built the first environment in which all three are met. On April 13, 2027, the engineer will walk out of the infrastructure he was building for twenty years. The network will keep running without him. On top of it, the AI for which the network was built in the first place will start to run. The miners who in August 2025 chose better economics in Monero will be choosing better economics in Aigarth tasks. That’s all I wanted to tell. Bitcoin was digital gold of the Darby phase. Qubic is the new gold of a phase in which, for the first time in human history, the computer has learned to work for the common good and not against it.
